subject: SIG: Sampling methodology + hotpatch SLA for critical CVEs
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@pegasusbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@pegasusbank.com
Date: Wed, 2 Apr 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: SIG request — sampling methodology + hotpatch SLA for critical CVEs

Hi Mina,

We're preparing the SIG/OE evidence pack for our internal auditors and need a concise description of Redwood's vulnerability scan sampling methodology for managed and dedicated deployments, plus a confirmation of your hotpatch/critical-CVE response SLA. Our ask: can you provide:

- A one-paragraph explanation of how you sample hosts/services for supplemental scans (e.g., risk-based vs. uniform sampling),
- The cadence you use for full infra scans vs. targeted sampling, and
- Whether Redwood can commit to a 48-hour remediation window for critical CVEs (CVSS >= 9) for Dedicated customers, and any exceptions (kernel/firmware/cloud-provider-managed components).

Also, please attach any short artifacts we can include (sampling matrix, excerpt from the hotpatch playbook). We want to get this into the SIG binder by next Thursday.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Asha Rao
Senior Information Security Manager
Pegasus Bank

Subject: Re: SIG request — sampling methodology + hotpatch SLA for critical CVEs

Asha — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a compact sampling matrix and the hotpatch playbook excerpt for SIG consumption. Below is a concise summary you can paste into the binder; I've copied the eng/ops leads for confirmation and any nuance.

Sampling methodology (summary):
Redwood uses a hybrid, risk-weighted sampling approach. We run weekly full-image vulnerability scans across all managed service images and a prioritized/stratified sample of multi-tenant host pools where full scans would be disruptive. Prioritization factors: public exposure, recent code changes, dependency churn, and CVE-intensity (hotspot libraries). Sampling strata and selection seeds are recorded and auditable — see attached sampling-matrix.csv. For Dedicated customers (single-tenant pools), we run a rolling full-scan sweep every 7 days with targeted rescans for strata that hit new high/critical findings.

Cadence:
- Full infra/host scans for Dedicated pools: weekly (7d) rolling sweep.
- Supplemental targeted rescans: triggered within 24 hours for newly discovered critical findings or when CI/CD deploys to production hosts.
- Baseline dependency/component scans: nightly (package-level) for commonly used runtime images.

Hotpatch/critical-CVE SLA (initial statement):
We commit to a 48-hour remediation or mitigations window for critical CVEs (CVSS >= 9) for Dedicated customers under our standard Dedicated contract, subject to the following exceptions:
- Exceptions: vendor-managed kernel/firmware (cloud provider appliance) and third-party hardware components where vendor patch is required. In those cases we provide mitigations (network isolation, WAF rules, configuration workarounds) and a documented escalation timeline.
- Conditions: SLA applies when Redwood has operational control of the affected component and when a confirmed exploitability assessment is performed. For CVEs requiring application-level code changes across customer codebases, timelines depend on customer coordination.

I'll let Kim and Ben add any operating constraints or changes to the playbook language we should include. If all good, we'll provide a short, auditor-ready paragraph and the two attachments.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 3 Apr 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG request — sampling methodology + hotpatch SLA for critical CVEs

Asha / Mina — confirming Mina's summary and adding operational clarifications for the SIG:

1) Sampling artifacts: attached sampling-matrix.csv is the auditor-facing export we use to show strata definitions, seed selection, and last-scan timestamps. It includes a short provenance column (scan job id, agent version).

2) Hotpatch window: we can confirm a contractual 48-hour remediation-or-mitigate commitment for CVSS >= 9 for Dedicated customers, with the following tightened language suitable for the SIG binder:

"Redwood commits to remediation or compensating mitigations for critical (CVSS >= 9.0) vulnerabilities within 48 hours of confirmed detection for components under Redwood operational control. Compensating mitigations may include network segmentation, temporary configuration changes, and WAF/rate-limiting rules where immediate code patching is not possible. Exceptions apply for vendor-controlled kernel/firmware and for third-party managed services; in these cases Redwood will document the vendor remediation timeline and apply mitigations."

3) Rapid validation & rollback: our hotpatch playbook (excerpt attached as hotpatch-playbook-v2.pdf) includes a 4-step blueprint: patch staging -> smoke validation -> progressive rollout (10%/50%/100% over 1–6 hours depending on risk) -> automated rollback triggers on error signals. For SIG, we included the smoke test checklist and rollback thresholds.

4) Evidence links: we will add the sampling export and playbook excerpt to the SIG folder and share the DocuSign clause we use for Dedicated contracts that embeds the SLA (link: https://docusign.redwood.example/ABC123).

If Pegasus wants a stronger (e.g., 24-hour) contractual SLA we can route to commercial — that would require a dedicated incident runway and calendarized on-call commitments. 

Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Operations
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Thanks — this is perfect and exactly what the auditors need.

I'll include the paragraph you provided in the SIG binder and add your sampling matrix + playbook excerpt. Two quick clarifications to close out: please confirm that the sampling export includes the last-run timestamps in UTC (we prefer UTC in the binder), and can you add the DocuSign clause id to the binder so our procurement team can reference it during the contract review?
